problems.statement: The non-negotiable 20-closes/day quota with leaderboard shaming rewards close counts, producing gaming (premature solves, ticket splitting, re-solve counting, quick-win cherry-picking) that inflates closures and the backlog while real resolution falls.
Closed-ticket metric is a gamed, rewarded measure: closes per agent rose from 11.7 to 19.0 while the backlog doubled, so the apparent productivity gain is largely artifact (repeat solves, splits).

Self-generated demand (reopens, split children, customer duplicates) is the main backlog growth: first-contact issues rose only 4% while splits/duplicates rose ~15x/6x and reopened, split and duplicate tickets make up most of the backlog.
Complex, valuable tickets are being starved by quick-win cherry-picking, aging badly and harming customers (CSAT drop, repeat complaints, renewal risk).
The client's framing that the bar is too soft or agents are not working is rejected: agents are closing ~19/day, near the quota, and headcount/hours are flat.
Insufficient capacity or headcount (needing 12 more agents) explains the backlog.
The Payroll launch flooded the queue and explains the backlog.
The reopen-rate rise is a measurement artifact from a changed auto-reopen rule (courtesy replies).
Attrition and pay (deferred pay review, Corvane competitor) is a contributing but secondary factor; quota pressure also drives intent to leave, and actual staffing has stayed near flat.
Rising engineering-dependent bugs (bank-feed API change) may explain part of the aging complex tickets, but the extent is unmeasured.

Removing quota gaming incentives restores quality: Team C's partial fix (not counting reopened closes) cut reopens from 24% to 10%, but splits and cherry-picking persisted, showing the metric design is the lever.

causalClaims.to: Gaming behaviours (premature solves, splits, quick-win picking)

actions.action: Replace the raw close quota with outcome-based measures (net resolution, non-reopened closes within 14 days, aging of complex tickets, CSAT), and stop the leaderboard shaming.
actions.rationale: Changes the established mechanism; Team C's partial change shows reopens can drop fast.

actions.action: Stop counting splits and repeat solves toward any target, merge/dedupe split children and customer duplicates, and restore oldest-first or priority-weighted queue picking.
actions.rationale: Directly removes the main self-generated ticket sources and cherry-picking.

actions.action: Run a targeted clean-up of the reopened/duplicate/split backlog and a swarm on aged complex tickets, starting with at-risk accounts like Larkspur.
actions.rationale: Most of the backlog is artificial or repeat work and is cheap to clear once incentives change; protects renewal.

actions.action: Link aged complex tickets to open engineering bugs and make the waiting-on-engineering status mandatory.
actions.rationale: Cheaply resolves the unmeasured engineering-dependency uncertainty.

actions.action: Escalate to a tougher quota with real consequences.
actions.rationale: Intensifies the rewarded, gamed metric and worsens gaming, quality and attrition.

actions.action: Approve the 12 extra agents now ($744k permanent, not withdrawable).
actions.rationale: Capacity was not the cause; added agents under the same quota would be absorbed by gaming, and the commitment is irreversible.

actions.action: Revisit headcount and the deferred pay review after incentives are fixed and the backlog is re-measured.
actions.rationale: Staffing need and retention risk (Corvane) can only be judged once demand is deflated.
Agents responded rationally to the incentive; punishing them targets the wrong party and suppresses honest reporting.

actions.action: Attribute the backlog to Payroll or to the reopen-rule change and act on that.
actions.rationale: Both rivals are contradicted by system records.

nextEvidence: Link aged complex tickets to open engineering bugs to measure how many are waiting on engineering
Pilot results from a redesigned metric (net resolution, non-reopened closes, aging-weighted) in a few teams versus control, tracking backlog, reopens and CSAT
Backlog and demand re-baseline after merging split children and duplicates, to size true capacity need before any headcount decision
output.summary: The backlog doubling is mostly self-inflicted. The rigid, leaderboard-enforced 20-close quota rewarded close counts, so agents solved prematurely, split tickets, re-solved reopened ones and cherry-picked quick wins. First-contact demand rose only 4%, while splits, duplicates and reopens exploded and now dominate the backlog. Complex tickets age, CSAT falls and accounts are at risk. Payroll, capacity and the reopen-rule change are rejected, and the unquota'd pod stayed stable. Fix the metric, not the headcount: do not toughen the quota or hire 12 agents yet.
